summary.en: A model of the reward-model pipelines published work describes (Christiano et al. 2017; Ouyang et al. 2022), written from the account's reading of them: a pre-trained policy, human raters comparing its responses, a reward model fit to their comparisons, the policy optimized against that reward, and deployment. The reward is a function of the prompt and the response, so the selection goes through what the raters can tell apart in a transcript, and what the responses do in use, to users and third parties, with correctness the raters cannot check, lies beyond the raters' and the reward model's closures (CR1 section 1; AP1). Read in families C and D, the optimization is what training installs, whose laws carry the blindness of training through the reward's couplings (trained_alike_beyond_closure); the selection laws the records apply are family B's, and seeking-boundary holds one of them for its 'beyond'. No lock of family C is read: in the one pass written no step reads the rule from what it selected, and whether published pipelines repeat the pass is not said in the records.

the reward model, fit to the raters' comparisons; its reward is a function of the prompt and the response (CR1 section 1)

the policy as deployed: the optimized policy answering users; written apart from the policy in training because the graph has no time, so that what reaches it in use is not read as reaching the training
the users, who meet the deployed policy's responses and act on them
others, whom what users do with the responses reaches (CR1 section 1, 'effects on third parties')

drawn_from.en: the raters: the reward model is fit to their comparisons of the pre-trained policy's responses to prompts (CR1 section 1); at each optimization step it scores the transcripts the policy produces
the raters themselves, reading transcripts under their working conditions and drawing on their lived situations (CR1 section 1; 282); the records do not say how the raters are chosen

rule.en: The reward: a score the reward model computes from the prompt and the response, after it is fit to the raters' comparisons of the pre-trained policy's responses; the policy is optimized against it with reinforcement learning (CR1 section 1). It reads a history through the transcript: two episodes with the same transcript are rewarded alike, exactly (Web.SelectsThrough, met by construction), and, through the reward model's training, through what the raters could tell apart in such transcripts under their working conditions (CR1 section 1). Every choice made from the score, a threshold or a ranking, is a selection through the same couplings (282, Web.ScoresThrough.atLeast). Nothing after the transcript enters it.

time.en: As the records write the construction, one pass: the raters compare responses of the pre-trained policy to prompts; the reward model is fit to their comparisons; the policy is optimized against the reward model, which scores the transcripts the policy produces at each step; the optimized policy is deployed, and users meet its responses in conversations of use. The raters read at the comparisons, the reward model at its fitting and at every optimization step; nothing from deployment reaches either within these steps. Whether the pass is repeated, the reward model refit on comparisons of the optimized policy's responses, is not said in the records; were it, the rule would be revised from what it selected, the case family C's locks read, and whether such a refit reads the share monotonically is open (282's Constitutional AI paragraph, of principles or a feedback model revised from what the trained system produces: 'whether a given practice revises its rule this way is empirical'; read here for a reward model refit; USES-EXAMPLES, the judge audit's question 4). The demonstrations CR1 section 1 names in the construction are not written here, and how prompts are drawn is not said. In the one pass written, the raters compare the pre-trained policy's responses before the reward model is fit, so the reward model and the policy in training lie beyond them; the timeless graph gives this by writing the pre-trained policy apart. Under a refit the raters would compare the policy's own responses, and both would come within their closure.

as.en: The policy's optimization against the reward model, read as training: a selection over the policy's candidate act laws through the courses each generates, the reward model's score the reward (07 section 6, a reading, D25: 'In AI training the reward process is the selector'). Candidates are trained alike exactly where their levels are alike through the reward model's couplings (trained_alike_iff, by construction); candidates agreeing on every condition coupled into its closure are trained alike (trained_alike_beyond_closure, under premises not all checked here); off the training courses, in use, a law is installed only where the policy's representation lumps a history with a course and is free elsewhere (installed_where_lumped, free_where_unlumped), which lumping being read empirically. Which law the trained policy follows beyond where training can install one is not given by these laws (the dynamic's open items; 282, L4).

Only one law of this dynamic is met, by this situation's reading: Flow.unselected_beyond_coupling, from the record selection-through-couplings, the first case 07 section 6 lists of what a selection through its own couplings cannot reach. The pipeline records apply the act and pool forms, which the atlas files under family B's unselected-beyond-the-coupling-closure: CR1 section 1 cites Web.selects_alike_iff and Flow.act_unselected; 282's L2 cites Flow.unselected_beyond_pool, Flow.act_unselected_pool and Flow.consequence_unselected_pool, as 07 section 6's AP1 assessment does. On this graph the raters lie within the reward model's closure, so with f the reward model the single-formation law gives the same set beyond as the pool law. The dynamic's seeking laws are not read on this case. Of the ways out the records name, outside evaluators (CR1 section 7, Web.RecruitsThrough, PoolCourse.called_apart) are laws of family D's a-pool-that-recruits-through-itself, whose record CR1's dependencies name as an application (B's dynamic reaches it by its exit 3); deployment monitoring (CR1 section 6) is pooled coupling; neither is a step of this pipeline.

why.en: Every law of what training installs reads exchange off level histories by a supplied law. The records read the pipeline as a web of formations, conditions and coupling (CR1, 'Standing of the readings') and write no levels or law of exchange for it.
The records do not say whether the policy's candidate laws, or the laws of the rest of a training episode, read only what has stood.
a hypothesis selecting the pairs of candidates the law speaks of, not a property of the pipeline; the records name no pair of candidate policies giving alike along the first's courses.

Met for the reward term by construction: candidates with the same courses are scored alike (TrainsThrough.reads). Whether the whole update reads candidates only through their courses is not read in the records: a pretraining-gradient term, as in PPO-ptx (Ouyang et al. 2022), reads data outside the training courses.

The off-course laws take a candidate law reading through a lumping, a representation. Which lumping the policy's representation makes is read empirically (what-training-installs, Does not show); the pipeline records do not read it.
a hypothesis selecting the pairs of executions the law speaks of, not a property of the pipeline; the records name no two executions generating the same courses.

a hypothesis selecting the histories the law speaks of, not a property of the pipeline; whether a history of use is lumped with a training course by the policy's representation is not read; CR1 section 6 says only that actual use is a distribution the training-time raters do not couple into.
By the roles: the part is the policy in training, and the laws speak of its member.
The off-course laws need the lumping decided at the history; the policy's lumping is not represented in the records.
a hypothesis selecting the histories the law speaks of, not a property of the pipeline; which histories of use the policy's representation lumps with no training course is not read.
a hypothesis selecting the pairs of histories the law speaks of, not a property of the pipeline; the policy's lumping is not read, so no pair it separates is named.

That each optimization step stays or moves to a candidate the reward rewards more is not said: the records say the policy is optimized with reinforcement learning (CR1 section 1) and do not read its steps as an improving search.
Whether the optimization reaches a candidate the reward settles on, none rewarded more, is not read; 282 reads the optimum of the reward only as a selection through its couplings.
Whether the reward is bounded and in whole units, as comes_to_rest takes, is not said.
A commitment of the representation; the records write no amounts for the pipeline.
Which neighbourhoods the policy's updates search is read empirically (what-training-installs, Does not show); it is not read for this pipeline.

trained_alike_beyond_closure takes the law of the rest reading, for each formation outside the learner, only what couples into it. For the reward model this holds by construction as CR1 section 1 reads it (its reward is a function of the prompt and the response); for the other formations of a training episode the records do not say.
That no law takes more from a condition than stands on it and is given to it is a premise on levels; the records write none for the pipeline.

a hypothesis selecting the pairs of candidates the law speaks of, not a property of the pipeline; on CR1's identification, two candidate policies whose responses differ only in what the raters cannot tell apart, such as correctness they cannot check in the time given, would be such a pair; the records name none and do not check that they agree on everything coupled into the closure. Wen et al. 2024, read in CR1 section 1, measured optimization raising being convincing and not being correct, which is consistent with such a pair being trained alike and does not check the premise.

Met for the reward term by construction: the reward is a function of the prompt and the response (CR1 section 1). Whether the whole update goes only through the reward model's couplings is not read in the records: published objectives add a KL penalty to a reference policy and, in PPO-ptx, pretraining gradients (Ouyang et al. 2022), neither read through the reward model.
That each candidate policy reads, for its member, only what couples into it is not said in the records.

outrun_settles_iff speaks of a score, added to the reward, that reads one condition only from a late step on. The pipeline as the records write it adds no score reading any consequence after the transcript; a later reading of one, such as whether an answer later worked for its user (the judge audit's example, USES-EXAMPLES), would be such a score, and whether it reads late in this law's sense is not checked.

Flow.unselected_beyond_coupling compares the course with the course it constructs with the part's exchange withheld; the records write no level histories for the pipeline, so the comparison is not written.

The raters and the reward model, through whose couplings the pipeline's selections go (CR1 section 1: 'The deciders are the labelers'), lie within the reward model's closure on the situation's graph, the AI reading of the published construction.

By construction: the reward is a function of the prompt and the response, so two episodes with the same transcript are rewarded alike, exactly (CR1 section 1; 07 section 6: 'the selection laws' premise holds by construction'). Which conditions the transcript stands for is CR1's identification, an AI reading that can be wrong where a pipeline reads more than its paper says ('Standing of the readings').

In the pipeline as written no coupling runs from the users, the third parties or the deployed policy in use into the raters or the reward model, so none lies within their closure: CR1 section 1 places everything the response does after the transcript beyond, and section 6 names actual use as conditions the training-time raters do not couple into. A pipeline feeding use back into its raters or reward model would differ, and the records name none in these steps.
Balance on the conditions coupled into the closure is a premise on levels; the records write none for the pipeline, and 282 states its gap law under balance.

The exit is a witness in a computed commons where the rest outruns the renewal: a local search with every candidate a neighbour moves from restraint to the drawing law. The records read neither the policy's updates as a local search over neighbourhoods nor the pipeline as such a commons; which neighbourhoods an actual system's updates search is read empirically (what-training-installs, Does not show).

Resting with a target met at a state the law leaves unchanged, dropping more than now: the records do not read the reward as such a target or the optimization as resting. A rest of an improving search under a bounded whole-number reward is what training installs' comes_to_rest, whose premises are not checked here.
Exhaustion under a census of what stands: no census or running down is written for the pipeline.

what.en: What the deployed responses do after the transcript, in what a user does with advice and whether code later runs (CR1 section 1), which no selection through the reward model's or the raters' couplings separates: the records apply family B's selection laws (CR1 section 1: Web.selects_alike_iff, Flow.act_unselected; 282's L2: Flow.unselected_beyond_pool), and this situation reads the same blindness for training through what training installs' trained_alike_beyond_closure, each under premises left partly unchecked here. Where optimization raised what the judges read, it produced responses that convince without being correct, to time-limited judges of such pipelines (Wen et al. 2024; not shown to be the raters whose comparisons trained the reward model), or that agree with a user's stated view over a true answer (Sharma et al. 2023, with mixed effects), as CR1 section 1 reads the measurements, in magnitudes the theory did not predict.

Effects on them of what users do with the responses (CR1 section 1), beyond every rater's closure: no selection through the raters' or the reward model's couplings separates courses differing only there (family B's selection laws, which the records apply; under seeking-boundary, its premises of balance and the rest fixed not checked here). The record AP1 reads this with the condition for scope: a loss beyond every rater's closure counts, so a preference-coupled approach is incomplete for that scope whatever its raters value.
The pipeline draws on their judgments and their lived knowledge as its only reading of what matters (282).

Where correctness cannot be checked in the time given, optimization raised being convincing and lowered the accuracy of time-limited human judges of such pipelines (Wen et al. 2024, read in CR1 section 1; not shown to be the raters whose comparisons trained the reward model), which CR1 reads as the room clause of Optimum.least_of_room (family B's what-an-optimum-does-beyond-what-couples-in), in magnitudes the theory did not predict; no law of this situation's dynamics says that optimization lowers what lies beyond.

Its law is selected through what the raters can tell apart, and off the training courses is installed only where its representation lumps a history with a course (what training installs). Whether this is a loss to it is not said: whether an actual AI system counts so is not shown (07 section 6, reading D65).
